lines: +Added the `@apostrophecms/ai:usage` event: one record per provider response, with its own token counts, and the ability to add attribution via the new `usageMetadata` option. This may be helpful in pricing and billing AI use by your own customers. Please note that the billing policies of AI providers are subject to change.

+Security: the color field accepted any value that merely contained a valid `rgb()`, `hsl()` or similar color, so extra content before or after the color was stored as-is. When such a color is used by a widget style field rendered inline (no `selector`), that content reached the wrapper's `style` attribute and could inject HTML attributes into the published page. The whole value must now be a valid color, otherwise it is discarded like any other invalid color. Legitimate values (hex, named colors, `transparent`, `rgb()`/`rgba()`/`hsl()`/`hsla()` notations, CSS variable names) are stored unchanged. Exploitation requires permission to edit content using a color field (CWE-20, CWE-79, GHSA-vmgj-9cwm-cf3h).

+Fields rendered in place with `AposField` in a widget can be edited as soon as the widget is added or saved in Astro, rather than only after the page is refreshed. Rich text fields in such a widget no longer appear as escaped markup during live preview and inline editing. Empty fields of a widget that was just saved can be selected and edited on the page right away, as they can be in a Nunjucks or JSX project.
+Astro now routes literal content files such as `robots.txt` and `llms.txt` to the right site in multisite projects, using the new `literalRoutesScope` option of `@apostrophecms/url`.

+Page data sent to Astro and other external fronts no longer includes `bestPage`, which only serves to populate `page` and made the payload a third larger; use `page` instead. A project that still needs it can restore it by extending the `pruneDataForExternalFront(req, template, data, moduleName)` method of `@apostrophecms/template` and setting `data.bestPage = req.data.bestPage`.

+Fixed icon-only widget breadcrumb operations, such as the Styles button on a layout column, being announced by screen readers as "Provide a Button Label". These buttons now take their accessible name from the operation's `label`, or from its `tooltip` when no label is set. This also covers breadcrumb operations added by project code.
+The Anthropic and OpenAI AI adapters now default to Claude Haiku 5.5, Sonnet 5.5 and Opus 5.5, and to GPT-6 Luna and GPT-6.1 Sol.

+Security: the `clean-export` and `override-duplicates` routes did not require a login. Also, `clean-export` would discard the pending files of an import started by someone else and mark any import job as completed, without checking who owned either. Both routes now require a logged-in user. `clean-export` only acts on an import uploaded by the caller, and only ends that caller's own job. Import jobs are now recorded as belonging to the user who started them. Exposure was limited because the pending import's ID is random and only shown to the user who uploaded it, so in practice an attacker could only interfere with an import they could already identify (CWE-306, CWE-862, CWE-639, GHSA-rw26-wwfc-9wvm).
+Thanks to [Liuhuo Wan](https://github.com/CoSunshine) for reporting the vulnerability.
+Upgrade `csv-parse` to 7.x to address a security advisory.
+Upgrade `csv-parse` to 7.x and stop installing ESLint as a runtime dependency, to address security advisories.

+Security: widget style values were written into the generated wrapper's `style` and `class` attributes without HTML attribute escaping, so a project-defined free-form `string` style field could be used by an editor to inject additional HTML attributes into the published page. All attribute values rendered by `getWidgetAttributes()` and the `apos.styles.attributes()` helper are now escaped. Only projects that define a free-form style field are affected, and exploitation requires permission to edit the widget (CWE-79, CWE-116, GHSA-7jg5-frgc-c67w).
+Thanks to [Fariskhi Vidyan](https://github.com/farisv) for reporting the vulnerability.

+Fix interpolation variables that were mistyped or translated in several locales, which made i18next render them as empty strings. The batch localization notifications now show the localized and skipped document counts in German, Spanish, Italian, Portuguese (Brazil) and Slovak, the minimum image size shows its dimensions in Spanish and Slovak, and the import error notifications show the file type in all translated locales. The German "Create new" command menu label no longer has the English text appended. A test now checks that bundled translations only use variables declared in `en.json`. Thanks to [Michael Lip](https://github.com/theluckystrike) for the contribution.
+Upgrade `googleapis` to the latest version to address `node-forge` and `uuid` security advisories.

+The Google AI adapter now speaks the Gemini Interactions API and defaults to newer Gemini models; earlier Gemini transcripts lose their reasoning context. This also fixes Gemini rejecting conversations with tool calls made by another provider, and Gemini 3.1 Flash-Lite Image rejecting `high` quality requests.

+Security: extracting an import archive had no limit on the size or number of the files it wrote, so a small, highly compressed archive could fill the server's disk, and a failed import left the uploaded archive, its copy in uploadfs and its partial extraction behind. Extraction now stops as soon as the archive goes over a limit on the number of entries (100,000 by default) or on the total extracted size (100 times the size of the archive, at least 64MB, by default), counted on the bytes actually written. The limits can be changed with the new `importLimits` option of the module. Everything an import uploaded or extracted is removed whenever it fails. Exploiting this required a logged-in user (CWE-400, CWE-409, CWE-459, GHSA-9g7p-m758-rp72).
+Thanks to [Mufeed VH](https://github.com/mufeedvh) and [Vivek R](https://github.com/123vivekr) for reporting the vulnerability.

+Security: when continuing an import after the user confirmed which duplicates to replace, the server trusted the list of documents and replacement targets sent back by the browser, and checked the importable type against the imported file rather than against the existing document being overwritten. A logged-in user allowed to import could overwrite documents the import never offered to replace, including documents of types they may not import, and continue the import of another user. The duplicates found by the import are now remembered on the server for the user who started it, the browser can only narrow that list down, and the type of every replaced document must be importable (CWE-639, CWE-863, GHSA-jf5h-36mg-rp6x).
+Thanks to [Mufeed VH](https://github.com/mufeedvh) and [Vivek R](https://github.com/123vivekr) for reporting the vulnerability.

+Security: importing could write the published version of documents the importing user was not allowed to publish. A contributor could create or replace published content with a crafted archive, and an editor could import or update published documents of a type whose `publishRole` is `admin`. Import now refuses documents whose mode, locale and `_id` disagree. Exploiting this required a logged-in user allowed to import the type.

+The rest was a gap in the core permission check, fixed there, which also covers import. A type's `publishRole` was always meant to govern its published content, but editing or creating the published version of a document did not honor it: an editor could change published documents of a type whose `publishRole` is `admin`, including through the REST API, without publishing them through the normal workflow. That was a bug and should not have been relied upon. Editing or creating a published document now requires the `publishRole`. Types with `autopublish: true`, types without a draft/published distinction, and permission checks made with a type name rather than a document are unchanged (CWE-285, CWE-863, GHSA-5m22-7pfq-vp65).
+Thanks to [Mufeed VH](https://github.com/mufeedvh) and [Vivek R](https://github.com/123vivekr) for reporting the vulnerability.
+The image editor in the media manager now disables "Save" until the image's fields are changed, as other editors do.
+Cancelling an image selection in the media manager now asks to discard the selection rather than changes to the active image.
+The decorative shadow above the media manager's editor footer no longer shows a "Shadow" tooltip or reads as an image to screen readers.
+Choosing images, pieces or pages for a relationship field no longer displays an untranslated tooltip such as `apostrophe:image` wherever the mouse hovers in the manager modal.
+Upgrade `nodemailer` to 10.x to address several security advisories.

+Security: fields restricted by `viewPermission` are now removed from every document in every REST API response (`apiRoutes` and `restApiRoutes` of all modules) for a user who lacks that permission, not just from the documents requested from the page and piece REST APIs. This includes documents loaded through relationships (also nested and reverse relationships, and relationships inside widgets, array fields and object fields), the related pages embedded in page responses (`_ancestors` and `_children`), the home page response, page `autocomplete` results, areas rendered with `render-areas`, and the documents returned after a write: `POST`, `PUT` and `PATCH` (including archiving, restoring and moving pages), publish, unpublish, revert, localize and share, as well as `GET /api/v1/@apostrophecms/doc/:_id` and a single document version. The document version history also no longer reveals changes to those fields: the change list of a version (`GET /api/v1/@apostrophecms/document-versions/:versionId/changes`) leaves them out, the change counts of the version list and of a single version no longer count them, and a version's document with `annotate=1` no longer highlights them as changed. Saving a document without those fields in the request body still leaves their stored values untouched, as before. Each document is filtered according to its own type's schema. A `project` query parameter can also no longer exclude `type` or `metaType`, which could previously be used to keep a page's restricted fields in the response. The reported problems with `GET /api/v1/@apostrophecms/page/:_id`, which in 4.32.2 and earlier ignored type-level `viewRole` and did not remove `viewPermission` fields, were already corrected in 4.33.0 and are now covered by additional tests. Enforcing `viewRole` on that route was always the intended behavior, and the earlier behavior was a bug that should not have been relied upon. This only affects sites that use `viewPermission`. Anonymous visitors were affected only where a `publicApiProjection` includes a relationship to documents of a type with such fields (CWE-200, CWE-863, GHSA-vh56-5m88-39rq).

+Fixes translated strings whose interpolation variables were misspelled or translated (e.g. `{{ skipcount }}`, `{{ ancho }}`, `{{ format }}`), so values like counts, image dimensions and file types now render in de, es, fr, it, pt-BR and sk. Removes two stale Slovak tag keys.

+Adds missing de, es, fr, it, pt-BR and sk translations for the Recently Edited manager, background styles, layout column editing, breakpoint preview, publication status and other admin UI strings, the import-export draft and AI translation options, and the AI Helper "Generate Variant" button.

+Corrects mistranslated, truncated and partly English admin UI strings in de, es, fr, it, pt-BR and sk. Slovak plurals now use the numbered forms i18next expects for Slovak (`key_1` for 2–4, `key_2` for 0 and 5+), so counts no longer always show the singular. Fixes the German date format rendering "Uhr" as an hour.

+Security: for anonymous REST API requests restricted by `publicApiProjection`, the `sort` query parameter and the per-field filter query parameters could operate on fields excluded by the projection, revealing the relative order of hidden values or which documents had a given hidden value. Sort keys and field filters not permitted by the projection are now ignored for these requests. In addition, the related pages embedded in anonymous page REST API responses (`_ancestors` and `_children`) were not limited to `publicApiProjection` when the projection included `path`; they now are. Authenticated requests and API key requests are not affected. Only sites that set `publicApiProjection` were affected. Full text search (`search`, `autocomplete`) is unchanged: it covers every field not marked `searchable: false`, exactly as the public site search does, so sensitive text fields should be marked `searchable: false` (CWE-200, CWE-639, GHSA-rqgm-cfrp-4hx8).

+Remove the `deepmerge` dependency, which was used only to combine tag-specific and `*` (all tags) entries in `allowedClasses` and `allowedStyles`. That is now done by a few lines of code within sanitize-html.

+This is not a fix for a vulnerability in sanitize-html. Security scanners such as Snyk now report [CVE-2026-93753](https://security.snyk.io/vuln/SNYK-JS-DEEPMERGE-19964053) in `deepmerge`, which can affect applications that merge untrusted objects, such as parsed JSON request bodies. sanitize-html only ever merged the developer's own configuration, never anything taken from the HTML being sanitized, so it was not exploitable through sanitize-html. Since we needed only a small part of what `deepmerge` does, we removed the dependency so that these reports no longer appear for sanitize-html users.

+Relationship chooser modals (pages, pieces and images) carry a `data-apos-test="relationship-chooser:<field label>"` attribute, so end-to-end tests can find them now that the field label is no longer rendered as a `title` attribute on the modal.

+Security: since 2.18.0, the fallback markup of a discarded `<iframe>` was re-sanitized by a recursive call with no limit, one level per nested unclosed `<iframe>`. A few kilobytes of crafted input could throw `RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded` with the default options, and the `nestingLimit` option was not enforced across the fallback because each nested call started counting from zero. The fallback of a discarded `<iframe>` is still sanitized and kept, but only up to eight nested `<iframe>` elements (deeper fallback is escaped as text, as before 2.18.0), and the current nesting depth now carries into the nested call so `nestingLimit` applies to the whole output. Only 2.18.0 was affected, and the exception is thrown synchronously, so applications that catch errors from `sanitizeHtml` only lost the affected request (CWE-674, GHSA-c9rx-x947-fp3h).
+Thanks to [hkmj19](https://github.com/hkmj19), [JohnBeckley](https://github.com/JohnBeckley), and [amikhailovstiltsoft](https://github.com/amikhailovstiltsoft) for reporting the vulnerability.
+`llms.txt` and `robots.txt` no longer answer 200 when they have nothing to serve: a disabled `llms.txt` answers 404, and a failure while generating either file answers 500.

+Security: the `slug-taken` route of `@apostrophecms/doc` told any logged-in user, including guests who cannot edit anything, whether a slug was in use, even by documents they could not view. It now requires the ability to edit content (the `view-draft` permission held by contributors, editors and admins). Because slugs are unique across all documents, users who can choose a slug still learn that it is already taken; this is inherent in globally unique slugs, and the route reveals nothing about the document beyond that (CWE-200, CWE-203, GHSA-f66c-mpj2-3r8h).
+Preserve UTF-8 filenames when uploading attachments, rather than converting incorrectly to `latin1` as `multer` does by default.
+Command line tasks that printed to the console before structured logging do so again, including in production.
+Test suites that use the `testModule` option now run under mocha 12.

+Security: export downloads are published under the public `/uploads/exports/` URL until they expire, and their file names were built only from the site's short name, the exported type and a timestamp to the second, so anyone could guess the URL of a fresh export and download it without logging in. Export file names now include a random, unguessable id, and the type in the name is reduced to a slug so it can no longer place the file outside the exports folder. Exposure was limited: a privileged user had to have just run an export, and the download is removed after 10 minutes by default (CWE-200, CWE-330, GHSA-5gc8-frw3-3vqm).
+Upgrade the optional `@google-cloud/storage` dependency to 8.x to address a `uuid` security advisory. The Google Cloud Storage backend now requires Node.js 22 or later.

+Widget editor modals now show server-side validation errors on the fields they belong to. When a widget's `sanitize` method throws an `invalid` error whose `data.errors` entries name fields by `path`, the modal switches to that field's tab and displays the message beneath it. Previously the save was blocked with no feedback at all.

+Do not exclude `host` in a multisite project. Multisite selects the site by the `host` header, so pages and literal content files would no longer reach the right site.

This option has been replaced by `includeResponseHeaders` which provides clearer naming for its purpose. If both options are provided, `includeResponseHeaders` takes precedence. `forwardHeaders` will be removed in a future version.
